g.text: thousands of threads, each one a TCB, each one wanting a CPU
each TCB carries what its thread
has been doing: time run, time
yielded, used up its time slice,
or a higher-priority thread woke up
one thread per CPU, and for how long
The scheduler is a function the kernel calls: given every thread and what it has been doing, it picks one per CPU.
It is called thousands of times a second, each time something changes: a thread blocks, wakes up, or runs out of time.
